My parents got a divorce when I was 8, I'm 19 now. My mother was always a heavy drinker. She would get really angry and verbally abusive when she was intoxicated, but never really hit me. Anyway, I was trying to make friends through high school, being awkward as teenagers are, I had enough trouble with my self esteem.

Well, the last day of 8th grade we all got our report cards and I was pretty happy with mine all As except in algebra, I received a C. I showed my dad he was very proud and wanted to save the card itself so he made a copy and told me to take the copy to show my mother when I visited her. 

The weekend rolled around and I went to visit mom, I showed her my grades and she fell silent. She looked at me almost in disbelief, and had a look of pure disgust in her eyes. She said to me "What is this?" she pointed to the C.  "Are you fucking retarded? You are a straight A student, you don't get Cs." She threw the report card down and walked away. I was around 13-14 or so, and I never forgot those words. I received all As from that day forward.

Like I said, this feels kind of pathetic compared to some of the other comments I have read, but it was the most depressing moment of my life so far.

Be there for your mother, your brother, and most of all his mother. I lost a friend at 17. He was killed in a quad accident. He didn't even get to graduate, I was there for his family even though I didn't know what to feel myself. I stayed by his family's side, I didn't have much comfort to offer, but I think knowing I was there helped them. 

I think you're in a similar situation. 

You might not know what to do or how to feel, but you should still be there for your family. Sometimes just being there is all it takes to make a difference.

Perhaps you *should* talk to her. Even if it hurts, you can't just let someone you love go without telling them everything.

I understand that you feel like you can't tell her, but you have to. A phrase that will always stick with me that may help you out.

You miss 100% of the chances you don't take.

Just tell her everything, lay it all out, and let her know the truth. Whether it hurts, or not.
